details: For every nonempty finite binary concept class, $\log_2|\mathcal H|\geq2\,\mathrm{RL}(\mathcal H)$.
proof: Distinct leaves of a shattered tree require distinct realizing hypotheses, so it has at most $|\mathcal H|$ leaves. A uniform random root-to-leaf walk reaches a leaf at depth d with probability $2^{-d}$; its expected depth is therefore the entropy of this leaf distribution, at most $\log_2|\mathcal H|$. Divide by two and take the supremum over shattered trees.
proof_source: Definition 1 of \cite{filmus2023randomized}, followed by the elementary leaf-entropy bound.
name: Log Size / Randomized Littlestone Dimension
witness_verification: For the family #classes/singletons with n>=4, the established endpoint values or bounds, in parameter order, are $\log_2 n$ and $1-2^{1-n}$. The first parameter divided by one plus the second tends to infinity as n tends to infinity, ruling out every reverse affine-linear bound. See the database-owned value proofs for these two endpoints.
